We've now explored and settled **17 scenarios** — the original ten plus the six areas you added, and edge cases for all of them. Here's the full scope, in plain terms:

**Core**
1. Effortless save with auto-filled details, reviewed before saving
2. Your tags and formatted note, editable later
3. Powerful search (`#tag`, `"phrases"`, `AND/OR/NOT`, clickable tags)
4. To read vs Finished, library opens on All
5. Archive (reversible) and Delete (confirmed, permanent)
6. No duplicates — re-saving opens the existing one to edit

**Added since**
7. Opening the original page in a new tab
8. Multi-select and bulk actions — including "everything that matches"
9. Automatic preserved copy of each page (PDF kept as PDF), optional Internet Archive
10. Reusable live collections (text + include/exclude tags)
11. Import browser bookmarks / export the standard bookmark file (with your extras)
12. Personal display preferences (text size, density, items-per-load, default sort)

**Robustness** — first-run welcome, unreadable pages, long content, empty views, large libraries with whole-collection search/filter/sort, and the import/bulk/archive/dead-link edge cases.

I've also filed quality items for later (storage growth from copies, Internet Archive being a third-party dependency, keeping background work non-blocking, a concrete speed target, phone usability) and one later-cycle idea (dead-link detection). None block us.

I believe we've now explored the goal thoroughly and your recent reactions are confirming rather than reshaping. **So I'd like to switch from facilitator to implementer and build this — the real, running application covering exactly these 17 settled scenarios. May I start building it?**

(As before, I won't begin until you say so — and per our agreed scope, anything genuinely new that comes up while building I'll record for a later cycle rather than expand into now.)
